exposure: complete blood count parameters (e.g., neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio)
outcome: severity of transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN)
cohort: 62 neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit with a diagnosis of transient tachypnea of thewnewborn (TTN) were included, divided into mild (n=31) and severe (n=31) groups based on Silverman scoring.
finding: Serum lipoxin A4 and resolvin D1 levels were significantly higher in the mild TTN group compared to the severe group, suggesting a protective role, and resolvin D1 and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio were identified as significant predictors of severe TTN.
